history.p: The Magnificat was composed for Neukirche and performed there in 1730, that is while Scheibe was still living in Leipzig. This is supported by the fact that the copyist of both score and parts, Christian Gottlob Meissner (1707–60), was employed in Geithain in July 1731, and the transcription must therefore have taken place before he left Leipzig in mid-1731. It is possible that the work might have been commissioned by the church organist Carl Gotthelf Gerlach. In 1761, Breitkopf acquired the manuscript and performance material from the estate of Gerlach, who was the organist of the church, and at the end of the eighteenth century it was obtained by O.K.F. von Voß-Buch who amassed a collection of church music. It is listed in two of the Breitkopf sales catalogues (1761, 1769). The present Magnificat is placed with several other sacred compositions with Latin text.
